sources.name: Current Elche A, B and C ordered stop lists
OSM-derived landmark anchors used for map projection

transformations.description: Creates the city profile from settlement name Elche and mandatory Wikidata identifier Q10509.
Captures the current ordered stop sequences for urban Lines A, B and C, keeping Line A's two published directions independent and representing Lines B and C as explicit circular patterns.

Projects route-map stop-marker pixels into approximate latitude/longitude coordinates with per-route affine transforms calibrated from OSM-derived landmarks. Shared municipal stop codes are unified into stable StopNodes.
Writes the established scenario schema, computes all asset SHA-256 values and the aggregate contentHash, and registers the scenario in the existing catalog.

Removes non-OpenStreetMap build evidence from the strict runtime StopNode sourceReferences field. No synthetic or falsely labelled OSM object identifiers are introduced; route topology, StopNode identity, coordinates and official-source provenance are unchanged.

warnings: Runtime StopNode sourceReferences are intentionally empty in this interim package because the transport-domain accepts only genuine OpenStreetMap platform or stop_position source components there.
BusElche municipal stop codes, Moovit matches and route-map pixel projection evidence remain build-time provenance; they were not mislabelled as OpenStreetMap source components.

The future Elche OSM projector must replace each empty sourceReferences array with genuine openstreetmap platform and/or stop-position references before this dataset is treated as a production geospatial scenario.
This is a workflow goal/reference artifact, not a production-grade geospatial dataset.
The A, B and C stop orders are complete as captured from current public route pages on 2026-07-21.
Stop coordinates are provisional affine projections from current route-map marker positions and OSM-derived landmark anchors; they are not surveyed boarding-point coordinates.
The future automated workflow should replace these positions with canonical OpenStreetMap platform plus stop_position projections where available.

OpenStreetMap relations 1835858, 1835925 and 1837445 exist for A, B and C, but the public OSM route inventory reports mixed or partial route/stop completeness; they were treated as secondary evidence.
Line A retains two independent published direction patterns and no reverse pattern is inferred.
Lines B and C are stored without repeating the first StopNode at the end; closesLoop=true adds the final-to-first edge exactly once.
Municipal stop code is the stable identity within this goal package. A future OSM-based creator must preserve these IDs through an identity registry or emit an explicit migration.
No source route-map image is distributed in the scenario package.
Review source terms and ODbL obligations before public or commercial distribution of a derived database.
